content.comment_body: Hello! I have a question regarding the [product_name] module intended for PT100 temperature measurement. I am considering using it to monitor the temperature of a power generator. I haven't purchased the PT100 module yet and would like to know if I still need to connect a temperature sensor to it, or does the module function as a sensor itself? Also, where should I install the module to accurately measure the generator's temperature? Any advice would be appreciated. Thank you!

Yes, you need to buy a PT100 sensor. The module is designed for direct connection with a sensor. For best results, place the sensor in the return line from the engine 'head' to the radiator. Additionally, it's advisable to use a flow or level sensor at the water reservoir. This setup lets you read the temperature, and if there is belt failure or water loss, it helps protect the engine.

Thank you for the information. I'd like to mention that I'm using a 5KVA generator for home use, which doesn't have a radiator system. Could you advise on which battery voltage sensors are compatible with [product_name]? I want to measure the battery voltage used to start the generator. Also, could you share the price of the AM2 PT100 module? If I'm using the 12/24 V version with 4 analog inputs, is it possible to connect a temperature sensor to any of these inputs?

First, please avoid posting the same question multiple times so that moderators can manage the forums efficiently. Now to your questions: If your engine is air-cooled, you may not need a PT100 sensor unless you plan to display temperature data. You could consider thermostats that fit into the cylinder head and provide a NO/NC contact, which can then be connected to [product_name] (similar to those used in small transformers or welding equipment). You can find such products online, e.g. [url]. For measuring battery voltage, you'll need a converter from 12 or 24 V DC to 0–10 V, such as those described at [url] (refer to 'interface technology', page 1–37). There are other solutions too, like battery chargers with auxiliary contacts: [url]. The AM PT100 module is typically around 100 Euros, but using a PT100 to 0–10 V converter is less expensive if you have an analog input available. Best of luck.

Sorry for reposting the same question; I just wanted to reach more people who might have insights. Your help has been very valuable. I recently designed an AMF and ATS panel and interfaced it using [product_name]. My challenge is measuring both temperature and battery voltage. There are four analog inputs available – I can connect a battery voltage sensor to one of them, but I'm unsure about PT100 integration. Why is there a separate module for PT100 sensors instead of connecting them directly to an analog input? Can I use a PT100 with one of the existing analog inputs just to display the machine's temperature, without needing the dedicated PT100 module? I'm working on a cost-sensitive project involving ATS, AMF, temperature, and battery voltage sensors with [product_name] 12/24 version. Thank you for your continued support, and apologies for my earlier mistake.

If I connect thermostats to the engine cylinder and interface them with [product_name], will their status be displayed as temperature readings? By using thermostats, do I still need the AM PT100 module, or can I connect them directly to the analog input?

If you have a PT100 sensor, there are two ways to connect it to [product_name]: (a) use the dedicated PT100 module; (b) use a PT100-to-0–10 V converter. Both options allow temperature readings from the analog input, letting you display or monitor the values. If you use a bimetallic or contact-type thermostat, you'll connect it via a digital input. In this case, you can only detect on/off states, not actual temperature values.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are uncertain about how to integrate PT100 and battery voltage sensors with [product_name] hardware. They ask whether the dedicated PT100 module is mandatory or if sensors can connect directly to analog inputs for temperature reading and display. Additionally, users seek pricing information and want advice on compatible voltage sensors. The discussion highlights a need for clearer documentation about module functions, sensor compatibility, and system integration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want clear, simple instructions for wiring temperature and voltage sensors with [product_name] modules. They expect clarification about when expansion modules are necessary and reassurance that their setup will allow direct temperature display and reliable battery voltage monitoring.
